hypotheses.statement: Exact-mode storage comparison is unusable cross-platform for any state: EVM/solc uses sequential 32-byte slots (big-endian, length-tagged short/long string packing, keccak-derived long-data slots) while solang/pallet-contracts uses hash-based storage keys with little-endian SCALE values, so every write produces STORAGE_MISMATCH entries that are pure oracle artifacts, not behavioral bugs.

evidence.note: Steps 0/2/4 STORAGE_MISMATCH: EVM count at slot 2 big-endian, string long-form packing at keccak slot; polkadot count at hash-key 0x9d72... little-endian 0x01.., same string bytes stored contiguously at 0xff0f... key. Data content equivalent, layout fundamentally different.

hypotheses.next_probe: Re-run a minimal write-then-read probe (setString("x"), getString()) with oracle.storage set to functional/getter-based comparison instead of exact; expect PASS, confirming the mismatch vanishes when storage layout is abstracted away.

hypotheses.statement: The polkadot dry-run decoder serializes returned `bytes` as a raw string when the content is valid UTF-8 (including the empty case, where it emits "" vs EVM's "0x") but falls back to 0x-hex for non-UTF-8 content (e.g. 0xff matched on both sides). String returns are unaffected. This is a pure representation artifact, not a content divergence.

evidence.note: Step 5 RETURN_MISMATCH: evm "0x000102...1f20" vs polkadot "\u0000\u0001..." — byte-for-byte identical content, different serialization. Meanwhile getString (steps 1/3), concatRound with non-ASCII (héllo wörld → π), and bytesConcat all matched, so only bytes-typed returns diverge in representation.

hypotheses.next_probe: Query getBytes after setBytes("0xdeadbeef") and compare decoded byte arrays rather than surface representations (normalize hex-decode EVM side, charCode the polkadot side); also include a getString query with non-ASCII text in the same probe as a control, expecting string PASS and bytes representation-only mismatch.

hypotheses.statement: String semantics agree across toolchains: empty string, 32-byte (long-form, >31 byte) strings, and non-ASCII multi-byte UTF-8 concatenation all round-trip identically, including empty-bytes concatenation with 32-byte input — no divergence found in encoding/decoding behavior itself.

evidence.note: All query-level results agreed: empty setString/getString, 32-char string round-trip, concatRound('héllo wörld ', '→ π 0123...X') with multi-byte UTF-8, bytesConcat('0x', 32 bytes) — only storage-layout and bytes-return-serialization artifacts diverged.

Steps 0-3 clean: 31-byte ('abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzabcde') and 32-byte ('...abcdef') strings both round-tripped identically across solc and solang with functional storage oracle — crossing solc's short/long storage threshold produced no behavioral divergence. The only mismatch was the known bytes-return serialization artifact at step 5.

hypotheses.next_probe: Push the boundary with strings of exactly 31 vs 32 bytes (solc short/long storage threshold), and bytes length 0 vs 1, querying getters only with functional storage oracle; a PASS here would confirm even the threshold-crossing semantics agree.
